title: How a language model generates text: tokens, embeddings and context

videos.script: A model does one thing. Given some text, it scores every possible next piece of text. {{distribution}} Then something picks one piece, adds it to the text, and asks again. That loop writes every reply you have ever read from a model. {{loop}} In this lesson you watch the loop run, on a model small enough to look inside. You see text cut into tokens, which is what every price and every limit is counted in. {{tokens}} You turn sentences into vectors and see which ones land close together, and where that goes wrong. {{vectors}} And you see what a conversation really sends, because the model remembers nothing between requests. {{context}} At the end you meet the lab. One computer, one project, and a stand-in for the model provider. The line between what is real and what the course wrote is drawn in that section, and every lesson after it keeps to that line. {{lab}}
